meta.title: Customer support escalation
meta.description: How a support request moves from self-service to engineering, and how priority customers skip the queue. Response targets are illustrative, not a real SLA.

summary.headline: Most requests are solved by the chatbot or a tier-1 agent; only reproducible product faults reach engineering, and every answer is written back to the knowledge base.
points: The chatbot answers from the knowledge base and hands over with full context
Tier 1 resolves account and how-to questions; tier 2 handles technical diagnosis
Engineering receives only confirmed, reproducible defects
Priority customers go straight to a named tier-2 specialist

facts.Escalation rule: Escalate when unresolved or out of scope

modes.name: Standard
modes.description: All requests start with the chatbot.

modes.name: Priority customer
modes.description: Priority contracts bypass the chatbot and tier 1 and reach a named specialist.

data.title: Customer
data.subtitle: Raises a request
data.description: Contacts support by chat, email or web form.

data.title: Chatbot
data.subtitle: Answers common questions
data.description: Searches the knowledge base, asks clarifying questions and hands over to a person with the conversation attached.

data.title: Tier-1 agent
data.subtitle: Accounts and how-to
data.description: Resolves billing, access and usage questions. Escalates anything needing logs or configuration access.

data.title: Tier-2 specialist
data.subtitle: Technical diagnosis
data.description: Reproduces the problem, checks logs and configuration, and decides whether it is a product defect.

data.title: Engineering
data.subtitle: Fixes product defects
data.description: Receives a bug report with reproduction steps, fixes it and tells tier 2 when the fix ships.

data.title: Knowledge base
data.subtitle: Articles and known issues
data.description: Every resolved case is checked for a missing or outdated article; known issues are published with workarounds.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: Requests move left to right only when the current tier cannot solve them. Switch to Priority customer to see the shortcut.

steps.title: Self-service first
steps.description: The chatbot answers from the knowledge base. If it cannot, it hands over with the conversation attached so the customer does not repeat themselves.

steps.title: Tier 1 triage
steps.description: A tier-1 agent handles account and how-to questions. Anything needing logs or configuration goes to tier 2.

steps.title: Specialist diagnosis
steps.description: Tier 2 reproduces the problem. A confirmed defect is sent to engineering with clear reproduction steps.

steps.title: Fix and close
steps.description: Engineering ships a fix and tells tier 2, who confirms with the customer and closes the case.

steps.title: Feed the knowledge base
steps.description: The answer becomes an article, so the chatbot can solve the same question next time.
